sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles (updated July 2015)

topics_and_locators.topics: Bloch-ball parametrization of trace-one self-adjoint 2x2 matrices; pure-state boundary; Pauli trace identities.
rays, global phase, relative phase, spinor rotations, including the 2π rotation/global-versus-relative phase example.
bipartite coordinates, Schmidt form and finite-dimensional entanglement examples.

sequential_reading.notes: All 53 pages, including exercises, read in physical order. The chapter is a complete available chapter. Source bracket convention is linear in the ket/second argument and is translated in qc_r2.md.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 3: Foundations II: Measurement and Evolution (PDF title page October 2018)

topics_and_locators.topics: orthogonal measurement, conditional outcomes, generalized POVMs and finite ancilla realization.
operator-sum/Kraus representations, instruments, trace-preserving channels, complete positivity.

sequential_reading.notes: All 65 pages, including exercises, read in physical order. Physical decoherence and measurement narratives are source context, not logical premises.

topics_and_locators.topics: Bell basis, Pauli correction semantics, CNOT/H Bell-state circuit.
teleportation branch expansion, Pauli byproducts, arbitrary input and reference-entanglement preservation.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 5: Classical and Quantum Circuits (updated July 2015)

topics_and_locators.topics: reversible embedding, NOT/CNOT/Toffoli, clean scratch and reversible permutations.
compute-copy-reverse uncomputation and reversible pebble-game space tradeoffs.
finite gate model, registers and circuit semantics, intermediate measurements/feed-forward and deferred measurement statement.
circuit-counting volume argument and state-preparation lower-bound sketch.
exact two-qubit universality, finite universal gate sets and Solovay-Kitaev approximation.

sequential_reading.notes: Preskill leaves the local-equivalence classification behind the entangling-gate universality exercise unproved; it is not counted as a complete supplier. §5.3.3 does not provide a detailed state-manifold proof, so the proposed QC24 theorem needs its own proof route.

sources.title: John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 6: Quantum Algorithms (updated November 2020; personal-use-only prepublication draft)

topics_and_locators.topics: reversible function-oracle semantics and phase kickback.
period finding, QFT, phase estimation, hidden-subgroup methods and Grover search.
Hamiltonian simulation, eigenstate estimation, MPS and QMA/local-Hamiltonian discussion.

sequential_reading.notes: The final sequential pass was pp.1-64. After detecting that a prior inspection call opened pp.61-64 before pp.43-60, pp.43-64 were reread consecutively. Efficient phase estimation requires initial overlap at least inverse-polynomial; the chapter does not provide free generic state preparation. Draft assertions and cited results not proved here are not adopted as suppliers.
